acquisition.why: Inbound via paid social/YouTube ads, influencer gifting and content is UK-legal. Agents can generate and rotate creative, but whether anything goes viral depends on taste and luck. Paid ads quickly use up a £300 budget [E].

delivery.why: Physical goods need sourcing, QC, UK product-safety compliance and stock. A 3PL or dropshipping can take the fulfilment, but the physical-world cap applies.

support.why: Agents can handle WISMO, returns and refund emails. Damaged-goods disputes need a human check.

scores.R_why: £300 cannot fund inventory plus ad testing. The examples date from cheap early-ad eras or rely on celebrity/UFC partnerships. Health-adjacent products like mouth tape carry ASA claim risk. Ricardo has 6-8 h/week for creative iteration. A small dropship test is possible, but the odds are poor [E].
scores.M_why: DTC gadgets are saturated and quickly copied by Amazon/Temu clones. Meta CPMs are high, and AI-generated ad creative is commoditised. Success depends on winning the creative lottery.
scores.one_line: Survivorship stories (Orabrush, Plunge, Hostage Tape) from closed ad windows. A sub-£300, inventory-heavy, creative-lottery bet is a weak fit for an agent-run UK solo business [E].

acquisition.why: Organic short-form content is inbound and legal. Agents can clip and post, but audience growth is slow and depends on the algorithm.

onboarding.why: Followers and subscribers self-onboard on the platforms.

delivery.why: Original footage needs filmers at games, or rights to the footage. Leagues and events are physical. Only commentary or aggregation content could be automated, and it is rights-limited.

billing.why: Platform payouts and subscriptions are automatic. Sponsorship invoicing needs a human.

support.why: Sponsor relations, filmer coordination and rights disputes need a human.

scores.R_why: Overtime was VC-funded with roughly 800 paid filmers and owned leagues. Ricardo has no capital and little time. UK youth-sports filming raises safeguarding and consent issues for under-18s. Sports rights restrict reuse of footage [E].
scores.M_why: Niche sports pages are crowded. AI clip channels are proliferating, and platform algorithm risk is high. Some gaps exist in UK minority sports, but monetisation is thin [E].
scores.one_line: A scaled, VC-backed media story with no solo, low-budget path. It needs physical filming and rights, so it is a poor agent-run fit [E].

acquisition.why: Meta/Google ads and content are legal inbound channels. The farmers'-market half needs a human in person. Ad creative rotation (60 ads) could be agent-assisted.

onboarding.why: Ecommerce checkout plus a free pre-recorded masterclass.

delivery.why: Making and packing food kits is physical. A co-packer is possible but needs minimums and capital [E].

support.why: Agents can answer recipe and order chat. Allergen or quality complaints need a human.

scores.R_why: A dry-ingredient kit is low-risk food. It still needs council food-business registration, allergen labelling (gluten) and UK flour sourcing. Home packing does not suit 6-8 h/week with a toddler. £300 allows only a tiny ad test. The claimed margins are eaten by Facebook ad costs [E].
scores.M_why: UK pizza-oven owners (Ooni/Gozney) are a real niche. However, flour brands and Ooni sell dough products, and there is no moat beyond content [E].
scores.one_line: A first-hand, plausible story, but it is physical food production with ad-dependent margins. Delivery and time make it a poor agent-run UK fit [E].

onboarding.why: App signup plus right-to-work and ID checks.

delivery.why: Ricardo personally drives every delivery. This is labour, not a business.

scores.R_why: It is legal in the UK via Deliveroo, Uber Eats and Just Eat. Earnings are roughly £10-15/h after costs, well below the $30/h claim. It uses his scarce hours, and nothing can be delegated to agents [E].
scores.M_why: Courier supply is saturated and rates are falling. It has no scalability or asset value.
scores.one_line: A job rather than an agent-run business. It is entirely Ricardo's own time, so it fails the brief [E].

acquisition.why: A niche podcast/YouTube channel for UK pest-control owners is inbound. Cold email to limited-company pest firms is also legal. Many pest firms are sole traders, which needs care under PECR. Agents can draft content, but a credible host voice matters.

onboarding.why: Intake forms and brief questionnaires can be agent-run. A kickoff call for retainer clients helps.

delivery.why: Suno/AI can produce jingles with human QA. Retainer marketing (GBP, ads, website) can be mostly agent-run with human review.

support.why: B2B retainer clients expect a human account contact and results reporting.

scores.R_why: Ricardo can build this technically. A £300 test of AI jingles plus a few cold emails to Ltd pest firms is feasible. The retainer side becomes an agency with human load. The UK pest market is smaller (BPCA ~700+ members) [E].
scores.M_why: Suno has commoditised jingles, so the $2k price will collapse. Trades marketing agencies are plentiful. The niche gives positioning but limited TAM in the UK [E].
scores.one_line: The niche B2B angle and AI jingles are testable cheaply in the UK. However, jingle pricing is being commoditised and retainers pull Ricardo into agency work [E].

acquisition.why: Local SEO, Google Business Profile and Facebook ads are inbound and legal. Agents can manage these.

onboarding.why: An online booking system with deposits and T&Cs.

delivery.why: Each hire means delivering, filling, balancing chemicals, then draining and cleaning a heavy tub. It is entirely physical.

support.why: Heater faults and water issues on site need a human callout.

scores.R_why: It needs £2k+ in tubs, a van, storage, liability insurance and Legionella/hygiene compliance. Weekend labour clashes with a toddler. Delivery cannot be outsourced cheaply. It is far over the £300 budget [E].
scores.M_why: UK hot tub hire is established and competitive, but local demand is real in Bromley/SE London [E].
scores.one_line: No first-hand evidence, hypothetical revenue maths, and a heavy physical, capital-intensive local service. It is unsuitable for agent-run part-time [E].

acquisition.why: Cold email to UK limited companies is legal. Content and SEO on AI meeting follow-up are also possible. Agents can run outreach with a human approving.

onboarding.why: Integration with Zoom/Teams/Slack/CRM needs scoping, security review and DPIA/consent setup per client.

delivery.why: Once deployed, transcription, summaries and reminders run unattended. Each implementation needs human config.

support.why: Agents can handle 'reminder didn't fire' tickets. Data and privacy questions need a human.

scores.R_why: It fits Ricardo's technical skills and could be tested within £300 with existing APIs. UK GDPR recording-notice and retention duties apply. Selling to businesses still needs some calls [E].
scores.M_why: Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, Granola and native Zoom/Teams/Copilot/Gemini already do summaries plus action items, often for free. Implementation services alone have almost no headroom [E].
scores.one_line: The idea is hypothetical, with no first-hand evidence. The feature is now bundled into Zoom/Teams/Copilot, so only a hyper-niche integration angle remains [E].

acquisition.why: Organic TikTok posting is inbound. Agents can generate and post, but reach depends on the algorithm. The account needs 5,000 followers before the UK affiliate programme opens.

delivery.why: An AI video pipeline (Higgsfield etc.) can be mostly agent-run. A human should review each video for disclosure and claims.

support.why: Buyer support is handled by the seller and TikTok.

scores.R_why: Costs are cheap and it is technically easy. However, the 5,000-follower bar, TikTok's AI-content labelling and bans on inauthentic content, and ASA/CMA fake-review rules (DMCC Act 2024) bite. AI characters 'reviewing' unused products are legally risky in the UK. UK TikTok Shop GMV is much smaller than the US [E].
scores.M_why: AI-influencer affiliate spam is flooding TikTok. Platform enforcement against it is rising, and account bans are a single point of failure [E].
scores.one_line: Highly automatable on paper. But heavy platform risk, saturation and UK fake-review law make AI-character affiliate videos a fragile, compliance-risky bet [E].
